bridges.burden: Show why a loving God could allow the world's suffering within the complete Christian account, while engaging the evidential challenge.
Defend the relevant value of virtue, growth and relationships rather than assuming pleasure alone is the goal.
Explain permission and ultimate defeat of suffering without claiming that every harm is necessary or beneficial.
Connect freedom, nondetermined development and human responsibility to divine nonintervention.
Explain the role of continuing existence, animals and future recovery in the defense.
Clarify how the defense depends on moral commitments and logical possibility.
Give evidential reason to doubt that a loving God permits the actual suffering, without undertaking to prove logical impossibility.
Test whether allegedly higher goods justify suffering or merely repair it.
Test why preventable or unnecessary harms are permitted even if recovery is possible.
Challenge the application of agency and soul-building explanations to natural and animal suffering.
Critique the opponent's internal commitments without needing an independent moral-realist theory.
